XML well formed?
Example and Tip

Example: An unclosed element prevents the reading of a XML file.

Tip: Automatically check XML well-formedness. After that, further tests can work reliably.

→
schema respected?
Example and Tip

Example: The schema checks whether elements may occur at the intended location. A missing optional solution part can still be allowed.

Tip: Version the schema with the documented corpus model; check technical completeness additionally.

collection and references received?
Example and Tip

Example: After the export there are still two puzzles, but instead of two no solutions.

Tip: Compare expected units, identifiers and reference targets; examine each unexpected decrease.

Derivatives checked?
Example and Tip

Example: A TXT export with solutions has more words than just an export of puzzles.

Tip: Test expected components and exclusions of extraction on a small sample.

Places read against source?
Example and Tip

Example: The source separates puzzles and solutions, the conversion must get this relationship.

Tip: In case of changes to the conversion just read the affected source structures exactly.

approval documented?

Example: A pull request holds change, passed exams and technical approval.

Tip: Only record released changes in the next release; name known limits in the release notes.
